mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation of each corporate shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing jurisdiction is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, the registry copy or notarized copy must bear an apostille from that country's designated Competent Authority. If the issuing jurisdiction is not a party, the document must go through consular legalization by the New Zealand embassy or consulate having jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, mutually exclusive paths and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or equivalent certificate of existence) for each corporate shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apply the same single authentication path as the certificate of incorporation: apostille for Hague Apostille Convention states only, or consular legalization for non-member states only. No hybrid or sequential authentication is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing the New Zealand incorporation agent and authorizing UBO disclosures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of each corporate shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the directors' signatures in the jurisdiction where the board met; then obtain an apostille if that jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, or consular legalization from the New Zealand consulate if it is not. The two methods are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of Articles of Association / Constitution / Charter of each corporate shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or certified public notary of the source jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The certified copy must be notarized, then either apostilled (if source jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention party) or consular-legalized (if not). Use only the path applicable to the source country; do not add a second authentication layer.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for each individual UBO and each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualifying bank where the UBO or corporate shareholder maintains accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank must issue the letter on official letterhead and have an authorized officer sign; the bank's signature must be notarized, then the notarized document must be either apostilled or consular-legalized according to the bank's jurisdiction. The two legalization regimes are alternatives and may not be used in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of residential address of each individual UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the copy, then apply apostille (member state) or consular legalization (non-member state) from the competent authority/consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel; never apply both to the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be conducted on all individual UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, shareholders above the 25% threshold, and beneficial owners of any corporate partner. The screening must cover New Zealand Police, Interpol, UN Security Council sanctions, consolidated OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UK, EU, and New Zealand sanctions regimes, all applicable domestic enforcement/disciplinary databases (including IPONZ patent attorney disciplinary records), and anti-fraud watchlists. Foreign PEPs are automatically high-risk and require enhanced due diligence before incorporation; domestic PEPs are to be assessed on risk and approved by an AML/CFT compliance officer. Updates must be made continuously, and any hit must be escalated to the compliance officer and the NZ FIU within 24 hours.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official register language is English; Latin-script names are used without phonetic transliteration. Maori words and diacritical marks (e.g. macrons) are permitted in Unicode. The Registrar follows a four-tier practical naming review: (1) exact name uniqueness; (2) phonetic similarity; (3) English-language meaning / Maori translation equivalence; (4) addition of sectoral descriptors such as PATENT, IP, or TRADEMARK to avoid confusion. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into English alphabet for the register.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office rejects a proposed name, the applicant has 20 working days from the date of the rejection notice to file a formal review request through the Companies Register portal or in writing to the Registrar. The review submission must explain the distinctive elements, provide evidence that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing name, and include any consents from professional bodies (e.g. IPONZ for patent attorney terms). If the Registrar confirms the rejection on review, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under the Companies Act 1993. A name reservation may be extended by a further 20 working days upon a renewal application filed before the original reservation expires; no extension can be made after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A basic virtual office or commercial mailbox may satisfy the Companies Act 1993 registered-office requirement if it provides a physical street address in New Zealand and has authority to accept legal process. However, for an ISIC 7490 IP patent prosecution agency, Inland Revenue and New Zealand banks will generally reject a pure virtual mailbox because the business must demonstrate a real commercial substance, an accessible place where business books and records are kept, staff or an agent present, and a public-facing premises that supports the professional-services business. A serviced office with a dedicated suite, meeting room access, local secretarial support, and on-site IP attorney presence is the lower-risk structure; a virtual office without physical presence is likely to be rejected by banks and IRD for tax-residency and AML/CFT commercial-substance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) verify the registered office street address is physically occupied and signposted; (2) ensure business records and registers are maintained at or accessible from the registered office; (3) confirm licensed patent attorney presence and IPONZ registration; (4) ensure utility bill or lease in company name; (5) verify company phone/email on official letterhead. Quantified risk of unannounced inspection by Inland Revenue is low (approximately 5-10% annually) for a low-risk professional services office; Companies Office inspection is rare (under 5%) unless an annual return or compliance complaint triggers it; IPONZ may spot-check patent attorney premises if complaints or disciplinary issues arise.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 10 (name), 12-16 (incorporation), 128 (registered office), 131 (directors), 152 (share capital)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCN (Incorporation Application) and any accompanying consents
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No minimum paid-up capital requirement. The company may be incorporated with any amount of share capital, and shares may be issued at par or premium as determined by the board.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company') held at [Registered Office Address] on [Date] at [Time].

PRESENT: [Director 1], [Director 2], [Director 3] (all directors present).

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the Company's initial share capital be set at NZD 1,000 divided into 1,000 ordinary shares of NZD 1.00 each, and that the subscribers to the Memorandum of Association shall hereby subscribe for such shares as set out in the share register, and that the allotment of such shares be approved and recorded.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the Company open a bank account with [Bank Name] and that the following persons be and are hereby authorized to sign on behalf of the Company, either individually or jointly as required: [Director 1] and [Director 2]. The bank shall be furnished with a certified copy of this resolution and any other documents required.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [Address] and that the Company's address for service be set at the same address, and that the Registrar of Companies be notified accordingly.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that [Director 1] be appointed as Managing Director, [Director 2] as Company Secretary, and [Director 3] as Chief Financial Officer, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until their successors are appointed.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the directors be and are hereby authorized to take all necessary steps to comply with the Companies Act 1993, including filing all required documents with the Companies Office, obtaining an IRD number, and registering for any applicable taxes.

All resolutions were passed unanimously.

Certified true and accurate: [Signature] [Name] [Title]

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Companies Register to ensure the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name. Submit a name reservation application via the online portal, providing at least three alternative names in order of preference. The application must include the applicant's identification details and the intended company type. The reservation is valid for 20 working days. If the name is approved, proceed to incorporation; if rejected, the applicant will receive reasons and may submit a new name or appeal the decision.
required_dossiers: Consent from each proposed director and shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a formal objection with the Companies Office within 10 working days, or submit a new name application. The Companies Office will provide a written explanation for the rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form NZCN (Incorporation Application) electronically. Provide the company name, registered office address, address for service, details of directors and shareholders, and the share structure. Each director and shareholder must provide consent via Form NZCN-A and NZCN-B respectively. The application must be signed by all directors and shareholders (or their authorized agents). Pay the filing fee online. Submit the application through the Companies Office website. The application will be processed immediately if all information is correct.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (Form NZCN-A)
Consent to act as shareholder (Form NZCN-B)
Proof of registered office address (e.g., lease agreement)
Address for service (if different from registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, the Companies Office will issue a notice detailing deficiencies. The applicant may correct and resubmit the application within 20 working days. There is no formal appeal, but a new application can be made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Compliance and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and Inland Revenue Department (IRD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the company must maintain a share register, director register, and other statutory records. The company must file an annual return each year. The company must obtain an IRD number from Inland Revenue by submitting Form IR596. If the company's annual turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000, it must register for GST. The company must also appoint a registered office and address for service. All statutory records must be kept at the registered office or a location notified to the Companies Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number is delayed, the company can contact Inland Revenue directly. For annual return, the company must file within 30 days of the anniversary of incorporation; failure may result in penalties. The company can apply for an extension if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Professional Licensing for Patent Prosecution Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand (IPONZ) and New Zealand Institute of Patent Attorneys (NZIPA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a patent prosecution agency, the company must ensure that all principals are registered patent attorneys under the Patents Act 2013. The company must apply for a license to operate as a patent attorney firm. The application must include evidence of each attorney's registration, good standing with NZIPA, and compliance with the Code of Conduct. The company must also provide its incorporation details, a business plan, and a compliance manual. The application is submitted to IPONZ, which coordinates with NZIPA for verification.
required_dossiers: Proof of registration of each patent attorney
Certificate of good standing from NZIPA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license is refused, the company may appeal to the District Court within 20 working days. The company may also apply for a provisional license while the appeal is pending, subject to conditions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) – online portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz/my-ird)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a New Zealand limited company, the company must first be incorporated with the New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO). Upon incorporation, the company automatically receives a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). To obtain a Tax Identification Number (TIN) for income tax and GST purposes, the company must apply to the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) for an IRD number. The application is made via the IRD's online portal (myIR) or by submitting the relevant registration form (IR596 for non-resident companies). The company must provide its NZBN, certificate of incorporation, details of directors and shareholders, and the intended business activities. The IRD will issue an IRD number, which serves as the TIN for both income tax and GST. For GST registration, the company must separately register for GST if its taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period, or if it voluntarily chooses to register. The GST registration is also completed via myIR. Non-resident companies may be required to appoint a New Zealand resident agent for tax purposes if they do not have a fixed establishment in New Zealand.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance or e-invoicing mandate. New Zealand permits voluntary use of e-invoicing (PEPPOL standard) but does not require API-based clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping. GST returns are filed electronically via myIR on a periodic basis (typically monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: Zero-rating applies to goods exported from New Zealand within 28 days of supply, provided the supplier retains evidence of export (e.g., customs export documentation). Services: Zero-rating applies to services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the services are not supplied in connection with land or goods in New Zealand, and the non-resident is not a New Zealand resident. For intellectual property services (e.g., patent prosecution), zero-rating is available if the services are performed for a non-resident client and the benefit of the services is received outside New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) – New Zealand Customs Service
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank statement evidencing receipt of foreign currency payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue Department (IRD) may audit export zero-rating claims. If a zero-rated supply is found to be ineligible, the supplier is liable for the unpaid GST (15%) plus interest and penalties under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Penalties include a late payment penalty of 1% per month and a shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax shortfall for fraudulent or intentional evasion. Additionally, if export documentation is incomplete or false, the IRD may impose a civil penalty of up to NZD 250,000 for individuals or NZD 500,000 for companies, and criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment. Retrospective clawbacks apply for up to four years from the date of the incorrect return.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Putea Matua); no separate foreign exchange administration exists because the country operates a fully liberal capital and current account system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalised financial system. There is no exchange control regime; the Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not require prior approval for current account transactions such as trade settlements, service fees, or profit remittances, nor for capital account operations such as share subscription, loans, or repatriation. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible and floats freely against all major currencies. Capital and current account convertibility are effectively unfettered, subject only to general corporate law and AML/CFT documentation requirements. Profit repatriation is achieved through ordinary bank transfers after board approval; there is no remittance restriction, but proper tax withholding on dividends and non-resident interest may apply under double tax treaties. In practice, the only frictions are tax withholding rates and the banks' internal risk-based due diligence, rather than statutory FX approval. Export proceeds are not required to be brought onshore and no surrender ratio exists. Accordingly, treasury planning should focus on efficient SWIFT routing, transparent source of funds documentation, and compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender rules apply in New Zealand. Exporters may keep proceeds offshore or onshore in NZD or foreign currency; no mandatory conversion ratio and no prescribed timeline exist. Only standard tax record-keeping and AML/CFT obligations remain.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI viability is limited to ancillary payment services only. Wise is registered in New Zealand under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and can facilitate low-value cross-border collections and certain WIPO-related fee payments. However, a non-bank EMI cannot provide capital escrow-grade account safety, documentary collections, trade finance, or the same level of assurance as a locally incorporated tier-1 bank. Some New Zealand banks may treat incoming transfers from certain EMIs with enhanced scrutiny or require source-of-funds explanations. Therefore, the entity should establish a tier-1 bank relationship as the principal treasury rail and use a fintech EMI only for niche low-value outbound disbursements after the bank account is operational.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand AML/CFT legislation does not statutorily require directors to appear physically in-branch. Most tier-1 banks permit remote onboarding using high-assurance digital identity verification, but for a foreign-owned or foreign-managed company they generally require at least one principal director or ultimate beneficial owner to complete a video interview with the compliance team. A consular-certified copy of the director's passport, proof of residential address, a notarised board resolution, and a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation are typically accepted. In practice, banks accelerate approval if a locally registered New Zealand resident director or a reputable professional agent is appointed to support the application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by overseas trusts, nominee shareholders, or multi-layered holding structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete corporate group chart, trust deed and protector consent, certified benefit-owner declarations for every natural person above 25%, notarised passports and proof of residential address, source of wealth statements, a six-month bank statement for each material funder, and a written explanation of commercial rationale issued by a licenced auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume patent and trademark fee payments could be perceived as a mechanism for moving funds to higher-risk jurisdictions, especially where client identities are not fully disclosed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client engagement agreements, WIPO/PCT filing receipts, official patent office invoices, a schedule of beneficiary countries, evidence of professional indemnity insurance, and a sanctions-screening report demonstrating no UN, OFAC, or EU sanctions nexus across all counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared patent prosecution business and the expected transaction profile, such as unusually rapid inbound capital or frequent unrelated cross-border payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A 12-month treasury forecast, signed commercial contracts with clients, historical IP filing records, the entity's fee schedule, board minutes approving the transaction purpose, and an independent accountant's confirmation that transactions are aligned with the ISIC 7490 activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection with no clear economic purpose or capital verification trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholders' subscription agreement, board-approved capital allocation plan, bank credit advice from a regulated source bank, the ultimate funder's KYC profile, a source-of-funds affidavit, and a post-arrival capital verification certificate from a New Zealand chartered accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or loan capital should be settled via SWIFT MT103 from a regulated source bank directly into the entity's tier-1 New Zealand bank account. The payment must clearly reference 'Share subscription / capital injection for NZ_LTD' and include the company registration number. While New Zealand does not operate a formal foreign exchange purpose code system like certain other jurisdictions, banks expect the MT103 Field 72 or remittance information to specify the transaction nature as a direct equity contribution or shareholder loan. Capital verification should be performed by a New Zealand chartered accountant using the bank credit advice, executed shareholder resolution, deposit confirmation, and the company's registry extract.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for patent prosecution services can be structured through SWIFT MT103 for direct official fees to WIPO and foreign patent offices where the beneficiary bank details and currency codes are known. For more complex trade-related settlements, commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are available but rarely necessary for IP service fees. Domestic New Zealand payments such as associate fees and VAT-like operational expenses should use the local clearing rails operated through Payments NZ, principally the Bulk Electronic Clearing System or high-value clearing system, while international disbursements above the local threshold should use SWIFT. A fintech EMI such as Wise may be used only for low-value trial payments to certain patent offices where tier-1 bank costs are disproportionate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Customised NZD/USD spot and forward contracts with tier-1 banks for genuine commercial exposures
FX options and collar structures to protect against adverse NZD movements in large client fee collections
FX swaps for short-term liquidity management between NZD and USD/EUR
Cross-currency interest rate swaps only where a fixed-term foreign-currency liability exists
Non-deliverable forwards are technically available offshore but are not generally necessary because the NZD is fully deliverable and freely convertible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to Companies Registrar (Companies Act 1993, sections 208-213)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First annual return due 12 months from the date of incorporation; thereafter each year within 31 days after the annual return date, being the anniversary of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late filing fee is statutorily charged, but failure to deliver the annual return is an offence under section 214 of the Companies Act 1993; the company and every director are liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding NZD 10,000. The Registrar may issue a formal default notice, and if no response is provided within 20 working days, the Registrar may remove the company from the New Zealand Register, causing all company property to pass to the Crown and the directors to become subject to disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Income Tax Return (IR4) for a New Zealand resident company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the income tax return must be filed on or before 7 July each year; for a non-standard balance date, the return is due by the 7th day of the 7th month after the balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties accrue under the Tax Administration Act 1994: a late filing penalty of NZD 50 is imposed initially, followed by incremental penalties of NZD 50 per day or part period, subject to an incremental late filing penalty cap of NZD 2,500. In addition, late payment penalties of 1% of the unpaid amount are charged on the first day, 4% on the 7th day, and 1% per month thereafter, plus monthly interest on outstanding tax liabilities. Persistent non-filing may lead to garnunishment, charge over assets, and criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Audit Report for the company's annual financial statements (only for 'large' companies or where otherwise required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders and directors (copy retained in the company's records; not filed on the public Companies Register for non-FMC reporting companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the balance date, or such other period fixed by the constitution or shareholders' resolution, being sufficient to enable the directors to prepare financial statements and the auditor to complete the audit before the annual shareholders' meeting (or the date specified in section 203 of the Companies Act 1993).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor when required under section 199 of the Companies Act 1993 is an offence. Failure to present audited financial statements to the shareholders as required under the Companies Act and Financial Reporting Act 2013 exposes the company and each director to a fine not exceeding NZD 200,000; continued non-compliance may trigger orders by the High Court to comply, and in serious cases the Registrar may seek to have the company removed from the Register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under section 45(1) of the Financial Reporting Act 2013, an independent licensed statutory auditor is compulsory when the company is 'large'. A company is large if at the end of the preceding accounting period: (a) total assets exceed NZD 60,000,000 (approximately USD 37,000,000); or (b) total revenue for the period exceeds NZD 30,000,000 (approximately USD 19,000,000); or (c) 100 or more full-time equivalent employees are employed. An audit is also mandatory under section 199(1) of the Companies Act 1993 if shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares deliver a written request, if the company's constitution so requires, if the company is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, or if the company is required to be audited by another Act. Small companies with no audit trigger may elect an independent review (a 'limited assurance engagement') but must still maintain proper accounting records.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice (NZ GAAP) as specified by the External Reporting Board (XRB). Large and public-accountability companies apply New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS Tier 1); Tier 2 entities apply NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR); smaller and medium entities may apply Tier 3 or Tier 4 simple format standards for for-profit entities. Companies that are not large and not FMC reporting entities may use the NZ SME standard framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate public UBO register, but the Companies Office captures ultimate beneficial-owner information on the annual return and through changes to the register. Every New Zealand company must keep a share register containing the names and addresses of all shareholders and the full details of any trustee, nominee, or equitable interest holder where known. Any transfer of shares must be recorded in the register as soon as practicable, with the transferee's details physically entered; share transfers are ineffectual until entered. Changes in directors and registered office must be filed with the Registrar within 20 working days after the change. The annual return must confirm, as of the annual return date, the exact shareholding, classes of shares, names of all shareholders, directors, and the registered office address. If any UBO or shareholding change has not yet been reported through a material change form, the annual return serves as the mandatory annual confirmation of the complete beneficial-ownership data on the Companies Register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Document Copy Register (constitution, certificate of incorporation and material contracts)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,200 per annum for a standard registered office and corporate agent service in New Zealand
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per annum for a full statutory audit of a 'large' company; USD 4,000 - USD 9,000 per annum for an independent review engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax incentive at 15% (non-refundable offset); no free-zone regime; no patent box; imputation credit system available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return, filed via Inland Revenue's myIR electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 must be filed by the 7th day of the 7th month after the balance date; for a standard 31 March balance date, the deadline is 7 July.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the New Zealand IRD number, legal name and registered office. For a non-resident-owned agency, ensure the postal address reflects a substantive NZ presence; otherwise the return may trigger scrutiny.
Must match the financial statements. Early balance date changes are permitted only with Inland Revenue approval; a change to avoid one-off non-resident withholding assessments will be challenged.
Report all income sourced in New Zealand, including PCT administrative fees and patent prosecution service revenue. Any intra-group service revenue must be arm's length and documented.

Deduct only expenditures incurred in deriving assessable income. Cross-border management fees must satisfy the arm's length threshold under transfer pricing rules; otherwise disallowance plus penalties apply.

If a loss is returned, shareholder continuity of 49% must be maintained to avoid loss forfeiture. A non-resident parent cannot group losses with the NZ company unless the loss is transferred under s IC 5.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding tax declaration on dividends paid
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare every dividend paid to non-resident shareholders. The NRWT rate is 30% unless a reduced DTA rate is claimed; attach the non-resident's Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and beneficial ownership statement to the IR4.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest and royalties paid or credited to non-residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the gross amount, NRWT deducted, and the relevant DTA article. Claim treaty relief by submitting the correct forms (IR290/A) and substantiating true economic owner status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of DTA treaty positions and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each treaty jurisdiction from which passive income is sourced or to which outbound income is paid. A new claim for unilateral relief (foreign tax credit) or a treaty rate reduction requires detailed source documentation and, in the case of a UK/US/EU parent, a limitation-on-benefits clause check.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: NZD 250 upfront, plus NZD 100 per month of delinquency. Late payment: 1% monthly incremental penalty with an initial 1% on arrears. A fraudulent IR4 triggers a shortfall penalty of 150% of resulting tax evasion, and criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994 ss 143A & 143B with fines up to NZD 100,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign competent authority; (2) provide a written declaration of beneficial ownership to the NZ payer; (3) submit a completed IR290/A (Notice of Non-Resident Withholding Payment) before the payment is made; (4) rely on the applicable DTA article (e.g., US-NZ 5% on substantial shareholdings) and retain this evidence in the NZ company's records for 7 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT: interest 15%, royalties 15%. Treaty reduction commonly: interest 10%, royalties 5% (e.g., under the NZ-United Kingdom DTA). For IP-licence revenue arising from patents and trademarks, the beneficial owner must show that it is not a conduit and that it has ongoing CIGA in the residence state.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10 million aggregate cross-border related-party transactions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand's tax administration will apply the substance-over-form anti-avoidance rule (Income Tax Act 2007 s BG1) and the OECD 2022 Transfer Pricing Guidelines. A mere direction as a PCT filing agent without local employees, office, decision-making functions, or risk assumption is not suitable for profit attribution. The company must prepare CIGA mapping to evidence that the core income-generating activities and economically significant risks are performed in New Zealand.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deleting or understating gross fee income collected from clients on behalf of the patent agency and netting it against undisclosed shareholder loans, thereby reducing taxable income in the IR4.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Evasion penalty of 150% of the shortfall (Tax Administration Act 1994 s 141E); criminal conviction under s 143A, with fines up to NZD 50,000 for individual directors and NZD 100,000 for the company; in addition, a civil penalty of up to NZD 20,000 per false statement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil under s 34 TAA: a director can be made personally liable for the company's tax debt if the evasion was assisted, directed or acquiesced in. The director may be subject to a travel ban (s 107) and asset restraining orders under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009. Imprisonment of up to 3 years is possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company used for dividend stripping and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the NZ company as a pass-through vehicle that receives patent prosecution fees and immediately channels profits to a non-resident parent without commercial substance, solely to obtain a reduced dividend withholding rate under the NZ-Hong Kong DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The arrangement is void under the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG1 ITA 2007): Inland Revenue reconstructs the amount to reflect the true economic position, plus a shortfall penalty of 100% of the avoided tax under s 141D.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who implemented the sham structure face civil liability for restitution of diverted profits under fiduciary duties; a blacklisting notification to the NZ Department of Internal Affairs may block re-entry; criminal liability for fraud when the arrangement was dishonestly misrepresented to the IRD; imprisonment up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Systematic failure to withhold NRWT on outbound royalties and dividends
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying patent royalties and trademark licence fees to a related non-resident IP holding company without deducting NRWT and without any DTA relief application on file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The unpaid NRWT becomes a debt enforceable against the company, with monthly incremental penalties of 1.5% per month (s 139A TAA). A failure to comply with a notice can attract a civil penalty of up to NZD 20,000 (s 140A).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under s 34 TAA, directors are jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid NRWT and penalties. In addition, the director who knowingly caused the omission may be jailed for up to 1 year; the court may issue a travel ban pending restitution, and a personal bank account of the director can be used to recover the underlying withholding.
